chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah, from Muawiya, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-Hateem, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is what is between the Black Stone and the Door.' And I asked him (peace be upon him), 'Why has Al-Hateem been named as such?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because the people squash (hatam) each other over there.'

key_terms.الْبَاب: Al-Bab: The Door of the Kaaba.
key_terms.الْحَطِيم: Al-Hateem: The semi-circular wall area adjacent to the Kaaba, between the Black Stone and the Door.
key_terms.يَحْطِمُ: Yahtram: They crush or squash each other (referring to crowding).

ai.seo_question: What is the definition and origin of the name Al-Hateem in the Kaaba?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies Al-Hateem as the semi-circular wall adjacent to the Kaaba, explaining its name through the physical 'breaking' or crowding (hatam) of pilgrims in this concentrated area of worship. This definition aligns with the Shia jurisprudential view that the space within this wall is part of the Kaaba proper, thereby granting prayers offered there the superior reward of being inside the House of Allah.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’albat, from Muawiya who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about Al-Hateem. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is what is in between the Black Stone and the Door (of the Kabah)’. 
And I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Why has Al-Hateem been named as such?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because the people squash (Hatam) each other over there’.
en.sarwar: 12. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Tha’labah from Mu‘awiyah who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Hatim as to why it is called al-Hatim (clashing). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because people there collide against each other.’”
